findings.summary: Source verification accepts loss of one runtime-specific legacy WebSocket dispatch when another runtime still dispatches the same action.

related.detail: The frozen/current equality check removes every daemon dispatch_sources value.
The regression covers complete global support loss only, not partial loss from a multi-runtime action.

findings.impact: The frozen baseline records session.reasoning.set dispatch in both Hermes and Grok. Removing the Hermes dispatch leaves the action globally SUPPORTED through Grok, preserves the action ID/auth/contract fields, and passes verify. This is lost coverage hidden by the weakening.

repro.mutation: Removed the session.reasoning.set case from session-daemon-go/internal/runtime/hermes/adapter.go while retaining the Grok case.

findings.minimalfix: Compare stable daemon dispatch coverage, not volatile citation hashes/lines: normalize dispatch_sources to repository-relative source identity (or an explicit runtime/handler identity) and require every frozen identity to remain represented. Keep line numbers and SHA-256 excluded. Add a regression with one action dispatched by two non-grpcapi sources, remove one source, and assert verify returns 1.

positive_results: grpcapi is excluded from the legacy WebSocket scanner, and the focused grpc receipt-projection regression passed in the tested snapshot.
Two direct generations were byte-identical and had canonical content SHA-256 847bb8ef078eb265d1f5b4be1939c5c47b8a5b709921bc4ce64216e3bb29b8d4.

After removing daemon source, dispatch_sources, and content_sha256, the regenerated document equaled the frozen document; IDs, requirement/feature mappings, support, auth, callers, contracts, and all non-daemon categories remained exact.
Deleting the sole dispatch for session.approval.respond caused verify to exit 1 with the expected missing daemon action ID.
The existing new-entrypoint and tracked-script-deletion fail-closed tests passed in the tested snapshot.
